items.title: Anthropic Unveils Latest AI Models Ahead of IPO, Claiming Top Benchmark Spots
items.summary:
Anthropic unveiled the latest editions of its flagship AI models, Claude Mythos 5.2 and Claude Faible 5.2, on the 9th (local time).   
   
 The new models feature a generation speed up to 30% faster than their predecessors, the 5.1 versions, and introduce a "fast mode" that increases inference speed by up to 2.5 times while maintaining the same level of intelligence. [...] On the safety front, the company maintained robust defense mechanisms against cyber and biological risks while reducing unnecessary false positives by 55% compared to the previous version, thereby improving user convenience.   
   
 Despite adverse factors such as a sell-off in AI-related stocks and a scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Anthropic is reportedly planning to complete its IPO this month.   
※ Please note: This article was translated by AI and may contain errors. [...] AI performance analytics firm Artificial Analysis also assigned the models an Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (AAII) score of 65, easily surpassing the previous highest score of 60 held by Gemini 4 Carbon by a margin of 5 points, claiming the top spot by a landslide.   
   
 Anthropic's second-tier model, Claude Opus 5.5, ranked third with 59 points, while OpenAI's top model, GPT-6 Astra, placed fourth with 57 points.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 vs Mythos 5.2: What's New In Anthropic's Latest AI Models? | Tech News - News18
items.summary:
Users who need faster responses can also choose an optional fast mode, which offers up to 2.5 times faster token generation at a higher price.

Anthropic claims Fable 5.2 performs better than Claude Opus 5.5 across several tests covering coding, scientific research, business tasks, cybersecurity, robotics and visual understanding. On the FrontierCode 2.0 test, Fable 5.2 scored 49.1%, which the company says is the highest result among the released models it has tested. [...] The company also says Fable 5.2 can complete some tasks using fewer tokens than its predecessor, reducing the cost of running complex AI workloads.

### Mythos 5.2 Focuses On Cybersecurity

Anthropic describes Mythos 5.2 as its most capable model for cybersecurity engineering. In an internal test designed to identify known software vulnerabilities, it found 10.2 percent more issues than Opus 5.5 and 14.4 percent more than Mythos 5.1. [...] Anthropic says its safety checks found a low risk of the models behaving unsafely in high-stakes situations. The company also worked with the UK AI Security Institute, Frontier Design and METR before the launch.

It claims Fable 5.2 has improved protection against unauthorised model copying, reducing the amount of data collected by such attempts by 90 percent to 99 percent.

items.title: All the latest updates on AI data centers | The Verge
items.summary:
Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

  Read Article >
 This week in the big AI data center buildout. [...] Read Article >
 “We are a data center first company,” AMD CEO Lisa Su says.
 ## OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects

  Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials. [...] Read Article >
 ## OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas

  In an announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes.

items.title: Tech Tuesday: Google facing criticism over its latest plans to integrate AI into classrooms | WOSU Public Media
items.summary:
/

AP

The Google sign is shown over an entrance to the company's building in New York on Sept. 6, 2023.

Google is facing criticism over its latest plans to bring artificial intelligence into classrooms.

Schools may soon have to choose between allowing AI-generated answers in a Google Search or restricting students' access to the search engine altogether.
